analysis: The only change in this PR is a documentation edit at docs/provider/cli-reference.md line 52. It rewords the GLM video-input description. The old text named inline data:video/mp4 and data:video/quicktime URLs. The new text says an inline base64 MP4 or QuickTime URL, constant or variable frame rate, with admitted labels defined in MediaIngest.admittedVideoDataURIHeaders. Both texts say the video is sampled at 2 FPS and decoded target-only. No executable code, configuration default, key handling, attestation, authorization or encryption behavior is modified. The unchanged surrounding text still states that GLM image input gets no prefix reuse and that the encrypted SSD prefix store defaults on. I found no new attack surface in this diff. T-050 (inline video plaintext in provider temp files) is the closest threat entry. It is relevant only if the underlying media code changed, and that code is not in the supplied evidence. The doc now claims variable-frame-rate support and points to MediaIngest.admittedVideoDataURIHeaders. A later review pass should check that the matching source change keeps video decoding in memory or in private files, enforces size and duration limits, and validates the header allowlist. The supplied evidence does not show that such a change exists or is unsafe, so I record this as an unverified contract rather than a finding. Nothing here alters T-041 cache posture or the TB-002/TB-011 boundaries.
